methodological_rigor.justification: PRISMA-guided diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis with PROSPERO registration, PICO-framed eligibility, dual-reviewer screening, QUADAS-2 and NOS quality assessment, bivariate Reitsma model with REML for pooled sensitivity/specificity, leave-one-out sensitivity analysis, Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test, and subgroup analyses/meta-regression by imaging modality and algorithm type. Strengths include an appropriate primary statistical model for diagnostic accuracy data. Weaknesses: only 6 included studies, which the authors acknowledge substantially limits statistical power and subgroup inference; English-only inclusion; some inconsistencies in reported heterogeneity characterization (mixing AUC constancy with formal heterogeneity metrics); several studies also appear in the same Chinese population, raising possible correlated-data concerns not addressed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Addresses a clinically meaningful question (AI/radiomics for detecting bone metastases in lung cancer) with summary diagnostic performance metrics (pooled sensitivity 0.86, specificity 0.88, AUC 0.931) that support the utility of AI-assisted imaging as an adjunct to radiologist interpretation. Findings are informative but not immediately translatable given heterogeneity in algorithms/modalities and absence of external validation in most primary studies. Classified Oxford LoE 2a as a systematic review of mostly retrospective cohort diagnostic studies.

reporting_quality.justification: PRISMA adherence is explicitly stated with a flow diagram; PROSPERO registration is cited (submission ID 1134225); QUADAS-2 and NOS are used. Search strategy is described (keywords in Table I) and statistical methods (Reitsma, REML, Wilson CI, continuity correction) are specified with packages. However, STARD considerations for diagnostic accuracy primary studies are not systematically appraised, several supplementary tables are referenced but not shown, PROSPERO registration is listed as 'submission ID' rather than a confirmed CRD number, and a dating artifact appears in the methods ('literature [REDACTED] and end of December 2024'). No data/code sharing for the analysis scripts.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors claim this is the first standardized meta-analysis focused specifically on lung cancer and bone metastasis using AI/computational image-processing, which is plausible given prior systematic reviews (e.g., Papalia et al. 2024) cover AI in bone metastasis across cancer types. Incremental extension of those reviews to a more focused patient population. Subgroup comparison of CT-based vs scintigraphy/SPECT-based techniques and of AI/deep-learning vs radiomics/other is useful but limited by small study counts. Not a major methodological or conceptual advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript suffers from notable language and clarity issues. Multiple grammatical errors ('fallowed' for 'followed', 'inferior to be ruled out' constructions), numerical typos ('NPV of 0.972–9.991' clearly meant 0.972–0.991), and awkward phrasing ('The high NPV strongly indicates its reliable application as a screening tool') appear throughout. Several Discussion paragraphs cite references (e.g., Ouyang et al. 36, 41-43) on unrelated topics such as traditional Chinese medicine and cuproptosis in lymphoma, which seem tangential and inflate reference list. Figures and tables are cross-referenced adequately but at times inconsistently (Fig 2 described with different content in different sections). Overall presentation impedes evaluation in places and warrants careful copy-editing.

key_strengths: Focused question (AI image processing for bone metastases in lung cancer) with PRISMA and PROSPERO pre-registration
Appropriate bivariate Reitsma model for pooled sensitivity/specificity with REML estimation
QUADAS-2 and NOS quality assessment with transparent consensus process
Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses show minimal fluctuation, supporting robustness of pooled estimates
Useful clinical framing around high NPV (0.97) for ruling out metastasis at 5-15% prevalence
key_concerns: Only 6 included studies substantially limits power, subgroup analyses, and publication-bias detection
Numerous typographical and numerical errors (e.g., 'NPV 0.972-9.991', 'fallowed') undermine confidence
Discussion includes references on unrelated topics (traditional Chinese medicine, cuproptosis in DLBCL) that raise concerns about relevance and fit of citations
Inconsistencies in figure descriptions and mix of heterogeneity characterization approaches
English-only search and possible correlated data from overlapping Chinese study populations not addressed
Primary studies lack external validation, which the authors acknowledge but do not quantitatively weight
chief_reviewer.rationale: Reasonably conducted diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis but undermined by substantial copy-editing and citation-fit issues (including tangential references and numerical typos); fits a tier-3 imaging/AI journal only after major revisions to clean text, verify references, and tighten interpretation.
